newsitem.title: MEXICO: Chrysler to build $80 mln plant in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler to build $80 mln plant in Mexico.

text.p: The Chrysler Corporation will build an $80 million auto parts plant in the northern Mexican city of Saltillo, the Mexican state news agency Notimex said Sunday.
The investment comes on top of $300 million Chrysler spent over the past two years to build its new truck assembly plant in Saltillo, Notimex said.
Saltillo is near the industrial city of Monterrey, about 150 miles (240 km) south of the Texas border.
The new Chrysler auto parts plant will serve the Mexican domestic and export markets, Notimex said.
"This demonstrates our confidence in Mexico," an unnamed Chrysler spokesman was quoted as saying by Notimex.

Chrysler has built cars in Mexico since 1938 and currently employs 11,000 people here, Notimex said. Outside of Saltillo, Chrysler has three other plants in Mexico, including a huge complex in the central city of Toluca.

The company built 19,212 units in Mexico in the first half of this year, nearly double the production of 9,929 units for the same period last year, Notimex said, citing the Mexican Association of the Automobile Industry (AMIA).
General Motors Corporation built 30,753 units in Mexico in the first half of this year and Ford Motor Company built 16,131 units in the same period, Notimex said.
